subject: Sprint close + QBR capture: outstanding asks, risks, and exec follow-ups
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint close + QBR capture: outstanding asks, risks, and exec follow-ups

Morning team —

Quick synthesis from this week’s cross-functional sync (and one ask from the exec table): we need a concise rollup for QBR by end of week that highlights: (1) open product asks that materially affect commitments, (2) any regulatory/security exceptions, and (3) mitigation / canary plans for capacity risks.

Please review and add updates inline in the attached QBR_Risks.xlsx. My proposed approach below — if you agree, I’ll consolidate and send a single slide to the execs tomorrow morning.

Immediate asks (Irene):
- Marissa: confirm status of the UX change request for streaming fallback and whether it ships in the next sprint (impact: latency SLOs).
- Karthik: give me a one-paragraph note on rollout plan + canary thresholds for model quantization changes (we need concrete rollback triggers).
- Vivek: confirm whether Dedicated customers will see any routing policy changes when fallback triggers — any SLA concessions?
- Jonas: block time on Monday to present the mitigation sequence for GPU pool saturation scenarios.

Attachments: QBR_Risks.xlsx (tabbed: OpenAsks, ExecSummary, RiskMatrix)

Thanks — short updates in thread appreciated.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Sprint close + QBR capture: outstanding asks, risks, and exec follow-ups

Thanks Irene — quick updates from my side:

- UX streaming fallback: engineering confirmed today that the visual indicator and fallback path are complete; QA found an edge case with truncated streaming when client reconnects. Target: patch in next hotfix (ETA: 2026-08-26). Impact: minor latency blips for long-lived streams.
- I updated the OpenAsks tab in QBR_Risks.xlsx with a deliverable owner and the expected ship week.
- I attached a one-page mutual action plan we walked through in the customer call (Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf) — Sarah at Acme requested this be included in the exec brief as a signal to procurement.

Open question: do we want to proactively propose a small service credit/discount for Acme if the fallback triggers during their proof-of-concept window? Execs asked for that option. If so, recommend we draft the language and route to Legal/Finance.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint close + QBR capture: outstanding asks, risks, and exec follow-ups

Adding the rollout notes (brief):

- Plan: phased rollout with 2% traffic canary -> 10% staged -> 50% -> 100% (automation for rollback at each stage).
- Canary metrics (fail fast): 99th pct latency > baseline + 120ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
- Rollback: automatic if any canary metric fires; manual review for partial degradations.
- Communication: webhook to Ops channel + short status email to CS + exec ops if canary fires.

I added these to the RiskMatrix tab. Also: we should include a short note in the exec slide that model quantization changes have a measurable cost benefit (estimated 18% token-cost reduction) but carry a small tail-risk for quality regressions — recommend an eval-set check before canary.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Applied ML (Serving)

- Procurement asked whether the proposed service-credit option would be handled as a billing credit or a one-time rebate. We prefer a billing credit visible on the invoice.
- Timeline constraint: Acme’s procurement window closes 2026-09-03 for Q3 vendor approvals. We need the SOW and the final commercial terms by EOD 2026-08-28 to make the cut.

Sarah

Good thread — consolidating next steps and owners (finalizing into the QBR slide deck now):

Action register (owners | due):

- Engineering (Jonas): prepare a 10-min GPU-saturation mitigation demo for Monday 2026-08-24 11:00 PDT; include rollback sample logs.
- Vivek: confirm SLA note and any Dedicated routing caveats (we need explicit phrasing for the exec slide) — due: 2026-08-25 EOD.
- Irene: consolidate the ExecSummary slide and send to execs with a one-paragraph ask (decision: approve proposed credit cadence or refer to Finance/Legal) — sending: 2026-08-25 09:00 PDT.

If anyone expects slippage, flag here ASAP. I’ll include the decision point language in the slide: "Approve conditional billing credit up to one invoice period if fallback triggers during POC window (legal to finalize)".

I’ll also push the consolidated QBR slide pack to the drive link and HubSpot deal today.

Thanks — Irene
